subject: lion
reasoning:
I'm planning out a stylized lion build using the SDK, working through joint hierarchy and part placement with correct API calls like createBuilder, b.joint, and b.part for positioning and scaling.

I'm sketching real-world lion proportions and setting up ground-relative coordinates, starting the spine chain from the root joint at the pelvis upward through the chest.

Now I'm laying out the full skeleton: hips, chest, neck, head, and jaw joints, plus a curved tail chain built from a polyline of points to get a natural hanging droop with a tuft at the end. I'm then planning the four legs as joint chains from shoulder/hip down through knee, ankle, and foot.

For the legs, I'm naming each joint along the chain explicitly and making sure to avoid hyphens so they match the required naming pattern, while assigning front legs to the chest and back legs to the hips as parents. I'm also thinking through how parts like tapered capsules attach to the correct bone when built from raw path points.

Rather than using chain-based sweeps for legs, I decide it's cleaner to build joints individually with explicit parent relationships and then place capsule parts on each segment with the bone set directly, giving rigid uniform skinning. Now I'm laying out the actual joint hierarchy starting with the hips as root, followed by the chest and neck joints with their parent links and positions.

Continuing the joint chain through the head and jaw, I set the jaw's hinge axis and orientation vectors so it rotates naturally forward and down. Then I move into planning the leg joints—shoulder, elbow, and paw—for the front limb, estimating positions along the body and thinking about how to generalize this into a reusable helper function so I can mirror left and right sides without duplicating code.

Writing leg helper function...

I'm picking out fur colors for mane, underside, nose, eyes, and tail tuft, then considering paint techniques like countershading or mottling for the body's coloring. For the torso, I'm weighing whether to use a loft across chest-to-hip stations with bone references to the hip, chest, and neck joints to shape the body smoothly.

I'm placing the head as a sphere geometry sized and positioned near the neck joint, then thinking through how to add a surrounding mane using a darker-colored sphere layered behind the head.

Actually a sphere mane would hide the face, so I'm considering using a ring of small spheres arranged around the head's axis with a frame positioned at the head center, building the mane as a circular cluster seen from the front.

Still building the muzzle and jaw geometry...

Now I'm positioning the eyes with yellow iris spheres and small black pupils, then adding cone-shaped ears on top of the head bone, and working out mane ring placement relative to the head sphere's radius and center so the mane frames the face properly.

For the tail, I'm setting up a tapered bone chain running from the hips through three joints out to a tip, with decreasing radii, then adding a tuft sphere at the end colored darker to cap it off.

For legs, I'm defining the foreleg chain path through shoulder, elbow, wrist, and paw points, adjusting the paw's y-position and radius so the sweep cap lands flush at ground level instead of sinking below it.

For hind legs I'm laying out hip, stifle, hock, and paw joints with the hock pulled backward for a natural lion stance, naming them hip/knee/hock/hindPaw per side, and checking the root hip and chest parent positions line up correctly with the body.

I'm setting varying leg radii across four keyframes along each limb for a thicker upper leg tapering to a narrower paw, and adding a flattened sphere part at each paw tip using a non-uniform scale to shape the foot pad.

For coloring, I'm planning a countershaded coat with a golden back, pale belly, and a mottled dark-brown paint texture for the mane, plus a solid dark tuft color for the tail tip, and setting up head sphere placement with the eyes.

Now I'm working out the head details: a muzzle capsule with a nose, a hinged lower jaw, eyes positioned on the head surface with embedded pupils, rounded ears colored darker than the body, and a ring of mane spheres arranged radially around the head using a frame-based ring generator.

For the second mane ring I'm adding more spheres slightly behind and larger in radius to build up the mane's fullness, while deciding against a big hidden sphere that would clip through the body. I'm also setting up the joint hierarchy -- hips as root, then chest, neck, head, and jaw as children -- and naming the leg chains (foreLegL/R, hindleg joints) with mirrored x-coordinates for left and right sides.

Now I'm starting to write the actual module: importing the builder utilities, defining paint materials like a countershaded body tone and a mottled mane color, then building out the skeleton starting with the hips joint and chaining chest, neck, and other joints with explicit parent references and position offsets.

Continuing the skeleton, I'm adding neck, head, and jaw joints with aim directions for the jaw hinge, assigning roles like "spine", "neck", "head", and "jaw" to key joints, then building a tail chain from the hips with multiple segments and sweeping a tapered radius profile along it using the body material.

For the limbs, I'm setting up forelegs and hind legs as mirrored chains (left/right) with shoulder-elbow-wrist-paw joints, sweeping tapered radii for each, and adding sphere paws scaled flat to touch the ground properly. I work through positioning math so paw bottoms align at y=0.

Next I'm lofting the main body silhouette across hips-to-chest stations with width/height per station, then building the head as a sphere, muzzle and lower jaw as capsules, cheeks and nose as small spheres, eyes with pupils positioned to slightly protrude from the head surface, and ears as spheres placed on the head's surface using distance calculations.

For the mane, I'm using ring placements of spheres around the head and neck frames to create a shaggy collar effect, plus a tail tuft sphere scaled vertically at the tip. I'm double-checking geometry segment counts via a helper function, verifying sweep/chain overload signatures accept array radii and point arrays correctly, then finalizing by returning the root and preparing to write out the complete code.
